content:
Since the launch of the bumper case for iPhone 4, this type of product has always been popular among users, but nowadays there are fewer and fewer options on the market. Rhinoshield offers a good choice for those who want a simple, minimalist full case.

Apple finally added the bumper case back to its product line with the iPhone Air last year. I had hoped Apple would extend its bumper cases to the iPhone 18 Pro (like how they extended the clear case to the iPhone 11 back in the day), but unfortunately they didn't. While I was looking for other options, I came across Rhinoshield's Minimalist Impact Bumper case.

Key Details

The fit of the Impact Bumper case is similar to most other bumper cases—the protective bezel around the screen is relatively shallow, while the back is slightly deeper. The case has a unique design feature that I really like: it has dedicated support points that keep the camera plateau and lenses from touching the surface the phone is placed on. This is especially important for the 17 Pro and 18 Pro with their aluminium alloy bodies. This gives it more protection than a typical bumper case, and also solves the annoying "wobble" issue when using the phone flat on a desk.

However, the fit of the case didn't quite meet my expectations. Once installed, it feels a little loose, and the edges can easily flex outward. I'm a bit concerned it might stretch out over time. Even so, I don't think the phone would fly out of the case if dropped (I've accidentally tested this a few times). It's worth mentioning that the entire case is made of hard plastic rather than rubber, so hopefully it holds up in the long run. Rhinoshield says the case can be 100% recycled because it uses only a single material.

The case comes in three colours to match the iPhone 18 Pro body: white, blue, and black (sorry to those who like Burgundy). The blue I bought is close to the Glacier tone, but not exactly the same.

Drawbacks

The case certainly has its share of flaws. What I'm most unhappy about is that the buttons are very hard to press. For some reason, they've gone with an almost completely flush design, and the button structure makes the press feel soft and unsubstantial.

The overall material choice might also be a drawback. To me, it doesn't feel as nice in hand as Apple's iPhone Air bumper case, but some people might prefer this texture. Of course, I prefer it over typical TPU or rubber clear case materials. However, this material combined with the slightly loose fit seems to attract dust from your pocket very easily.

If you're using Apple's Wrist Strap or Crossbody Strap, note that this case doesn't have the necessary lanyard attachment points.

Conclusion

Rhinoshield's bumper case is far from perfect, and I still hope Apple will extend its bumper cases to other iPhone models. However, I ultimately decided to keep using this case, mainly for one reason: it gives me a near "no case" experience while not having to worry about the fragile aluminium body getting scratched or dented. As far as I know, this bumper case is generally only sold on their own website, priced at around US$30, which is not much different from Apple's US$39 case once you add shipping. You can buy the Rhinoshield Minimalist Impact Bumper case here. (Amazon listings pop up occasionally, so you can try there too.)
